author: research agent WW
note: Town waterway types for 1730, the parts they need and every map-sketch settlement mapped to types. Generated by research/waterways/tools/gen_waterways.py from ww_types.py and ww_settlements.py.

decisions.recommendation: add g, shore landing (harbour, beach, lake shore): 28 settlements (ports, fishing and salt villages, lake towns) fit none of a-f. Recommend YES.
c1 levee river / c2 braided, unbridged gravel river / c3 town river. The Oi, Abe, Sakawa and Fuji crossings have no bridge by shogunal policy and are a Tokaido signature. Recommend YES.
the Takase gets its own look (8 m, 30 cm of water, funairi basins), but it is built from a's wall, step and bridge parts at low heights; Fushimi and Ogaki reuse it. Recommend YES.

coastal canal towns (Edo, Osaka, Sakai, Nagoya if on the bay) sit at 1-3 m and their canals are cut below sea level, so real sea water fills them; everything inland uses pond models. Recommend YES, and a map rule: every a-type city touches the coast.

sea-level canals full, with exposed silt at the wall foot; the Takase and d2 street channels near-dry (no one keeps the intakes); moats full but green and lotus-choked; springs (d3) keep running. Recommend YES.

d1 gutters everywhere by default; a d2 mid-street channel only where sourced (Nakatsugawa, Narai, Tsumago, Magome, Suhara, Kamiyoshida's plot streams, Sakamoto). Recommend YES: a channel in every post town would be a modern Gujo / Tsuwano look.

willow at canal corners and bridge ends; pines on levees and moat banks; wild cherries only on the Sumida levee (1717) and at temples; no cherry rows along canals (Kiyamachi and Ogaki rows are modern Somei-yoshino). Recommend YES.
had NO castle in 1730 (built 1777). Drop it from CASTLE_TOWNS and build a post town + river port. Recommend YES.
Kano (Nakasendo, 1601) and Minakuchi (Tokaido, domain seat from 1682) were castle towns in 1730 but are not in CASTLE_TOWNS. Recommend: give each a small moat (f1) and gate, no keep. Low priority.
a stepped pond-model river and a pond moat need one small test (swim depth, the joins at each step, drinking) on the test island before the c/b/f build lists. Recommend YES, one short agent session.

types.name: City canal (horikawa)
types.what: Straight dug canal between stone or timber walls; the streets of Osaka and eastern Edo, Nagoya's Horikawa, Sakai's moat ring. Kura and open quays (kashi / hama) line it; many plank bridges.
variants: a1 main canal: 20-36 m water, dressed-stone walls, trestle or long plank bridges, kura-yashiki boat basins (funairi)
a2 back canal: 8-15 m water, rough stone or pile-and-board banks, short plank bridges, house backs with steps
a3 river kashi: a natural river used as a canal (Ise Kawasaki on the Seta, Fushimi port): kura straight onto the water
cross_section: Sanjukkenbori was 30 ken (~55 m) from 1612, narrowed to 19 ken in 1828 [S-30K]; Nagoya Horikawa 12-48 ken (22-87 m) [S-NGY]; Nagahori ~40 m, Dotonbori 30-50 m (today's widths) [S-OSK]. Game: 20 m and 36 m
between the Takase (7-8 m, a hauled canal) and the named main canals; Hacchobori / Kaede-gawa scale. Game: 10 m
carried loaded flat lighters (hirata) at low tide; must be deep enough to swim in DayZ
Hiroshima domain kura-yashiki revetment, Osaka: stone walls 3 m high [S-KURA]; the castle-side wall of Edo's outer moat along the Nihonbashi River is ~6 m [S-EDOM] (castle scale, not a canal)
open unloading strip between the wall and the kura or house row, with sheds (naya), stacked goods and landing steps [l02, l07]
timber sill logs (dogi) on piles ~1 m apart
found under Edo's moat walls on soft ground [S-EDOM]; shows only in the collapsed-wall abandoned state
types.edges: Dressed stone (uchikomi-hagi / kirikomi-hagi) for main canals, kura-yashiki frontages and quays; rough stone (nozura) on back canals; pile-and-board revetment (kui-dome: posts ~0.9 m apart with boards behind) for cheap banks, clearly shown along the Onagi-gawa [l08].
types.steps_landings: Gangi quay steps at every quay and at each kura-yashiki (the Hiroshima domain yard had stone walls + gangi + a 51 x 47 m boat basin cut into the plot [S-KURA]); plank landing stages on piles; short private step flights at house backs.
types.mooring: Timber mooring posts standing in the water at the wall foot; holed mooring stones set in the wall top.
types.outfalls: Street-drain mouths in the wall every block (gesui-guchi); Osaka's back-to-back sewers end here [OL U streets].
types.bridges: KEEP_CIVIC plank bridge (most; Osaka had ~200 townsmen's bridges), trestle bridge (the big public bridges: Nihonbashi, Tenma-bashi, Naniwa-bashi), occasional arched bridge. No stone slab bridges (spans too long).
types.planting: Weeping willow at bridge ends and canal corners [l07]; a single old pine at a quay corner (Onagi-gawa's 'five pines' [l08]); no cherry rows (Kiyamachi-style cherry rows are Meiji or later).
types.buildings: Kura backs straight onto the wall with water doors (Nagoya Horikawa, Ise Kawasaki [S-NGY, S-ISE]); Osaka hama frontage: kura-yashiki and merchant houses each with their own steps; Edo kashi: an open public strip with sheds and kura set back. Laundry is not done in city canals (tidal, dirty).
types.boats: chokibune, yanebune, hiratabune (flat cargo lighter), tenmasen; yakatabune as a rare hero (OUTDOOR_LIST U boats, section 7.14).
types.abandoned: Water brown-green; a mud-and-silt shelf exposed along the wall foot; a hirata sunk with only its gunwale showing; a chokibune swamped against the gangi; a flotsam raft of planks, straw bales and leaves jammed against a bridge pier; one landing stage with half its planks gone; weeds in every wall joint and a green algae band at the waterline; one pile-and-board section slumped into the water.
types.terrain: Channel cut (bed below sea level where the town is coastal), the quay strip as flat hard ground, bridge-end plazas (hashi-zume).
types.placeable: Wall modules, gangi, landing stages, mooring posts and stones, outfalls, bridges, boats, debris.
types.water: SEA: coastal canal towns sit at 1-3 m above sea level and their canals are cut below 0 m, so the ocean fills them for free (FEASIBILITY 2.3). Inland a3 (Ise Kawasaki, Fushimi) needs pond models.

types.water_short: pond (or a dry bed with puddles)
types.name: Shallow town canal (Takase type)
types.what: A narrow, very shallow cargo canal with flat boats hauled back upstream by men walking the bank, and side basins (funairi) cut into one bank where boats turned and unloaded. Kyoto's Takase (1611, Nijo to Fushimi, ~10 km) is the model.
variants: b1 Takase: stone-walled, 7-8 m, funairi basins
b2 moat-canal: a castle-town canal of the same scale doubling as a moat (Ogaki's Suimon-gawa to the Funamachi port)
cross_section: Takase channel ~8 m, water ~7 m wide [S-TAK]
'a few tens of cm'; normal depth about 30 cm [S-TAK]
house backs and a towpath just above water; boats are flat and low
haulers (hikiko, ~700 at the peak) walked the bank pulling on a rope [S-TAK]
Ichi-no-funairi; another record gives 134 x 16 m; 9 basins between Nijo and Shijo, about every 100 m, on the west bank [S-TAK]
~13 x 2 m, flat-bottomed, max 15 koku (~2.25 t)
types.edges: Stone-walled both sides (the funairi are recorded as stone-walled [S-TAK]); rough stone where it runs out of town.
types.steps_landings: Short gangi and plank landings inside each funairi; a few steps at the house backs.
types.mooring: Posts inside the funairi; boats tied bow to stern along the towpath side.
types.outfalls: Small drain mouths from the houses.
types.bridges: Many short, low plank bridges (one per street crossing); stone slab bridges where it is narrow.
types.planting: Willows along the towpath (assumed); NO cherry rows (the Kiyamachi and Ogaki cherry rows are modern Somei-yoshino).
types.buildings: House backs and inns straight onto the water on the east bank; timber, charcoal and rice merchants' yards at each funairi.
types.boats: takasebune (flat, 13 x 2 m); the local boat type OUTDOOR_LIST 7.14 lost, back in as a length variant of the flat cargo boat.
types.abandoned: With no one keeping the intake weir, the 0.3 m of water drops to a trickle between gravel and silt bars; takasebune lie grounded and tilted; the funairi basins are silted, reed-choked and hold standing water; a hauling rope still tied to a post; leaves pile against every low bridge.
types.terrain: Shallow channel cut, the funairi cuts, the towpath strip.
types.placeable: Wall modules (low heights), funairi corner pieces (= wall modules), gangi, landing, plank and slab bridges, boats.
types.water: POND: Kyoto is inland and uphill. The trickle state is cheap: a thin stepped pond strip, or even a dry gravel bed with puddles.

types.name: Big river through or beside a town
types.what: The river a town grew beside: gravel flats (kawara), earth levees (tsutsumi) with planting, a long bridge or a ferry, and river works.
variants: c1 levee-banked lowland river: Kamo, Sumida, Yodo, Yahagi, Tama, Sagami, Kiso: long bridge or ferry, levees with roads on top
c2 braided gravel river, unbridged: Oi, Abe, Sakawa, Fuji, Tenryu, Kamanashi: a wide stony bed with shifting channels, crossed by porters or ferry
c3 town river: a 20-60 m river through a post or castle town, one trestle or plank bridge, gravel bars (Totsuka's Kashio, Fujieda's Seto)
cross_section: the 1670 Kanbun new levee narrowed the Kamo to about 100 m, straightened it and faced it in stone [S-KAMO]
autumn low water leaves wide gravel and sand flats (kawara) [OL U water]
grass and planted crest; a road on top where the levee is the road (Bunroku levee, Yodo; mem)
Sanjo Ohashi 61 x 3 ken (~109 x 5.5 m, 1780 record), stone piers; Yahagi-bashi 208 ken (~378 m), the Tokaido's longest
Oi, Abe, Sakawa forded on porters' shoulders; bridges forbidden [OL N 'Braided gravel river', W 4]
knee to chest at low water (assumed)
the reason porters (and river stops, kawa-dome) existed
20-60 m bed, 5-20 m low-water channel, banks 2-4 m (assumed)
Hokusai 1804 and Hiroshige Tokaido views [l04, l05]
types.edges: Earth levees with turf; stone-faced reaches in cities (Kamo, 1670); stone-filled bamboo gabions (jakago) along banks and round weirs; timber crib spurs (seigyu) and groynes pushing the current off the bank; open staggered levees (kasumi-tei) on c2 rivers; Shingen-zutsumi at Nirasaki is an old survivor [OL W 12].
types.steps_landings: Earth steps with log risers down the levee [l09]; ferry landings (earth or stone ramp, bell post, waiting bench); porter platforms (rendai) and the river-crossing office on c2; a boat landing at river ports (Kuragano, Fushimi, Hirakata).
types.mooring: Stakes in the gravel; boats hauled up on the flats.
types.outfalls: Town drains and irrigation outlets through the levee (small sluices).
types.bridges: KEEP_CIVIC trestle bridge at hero length (Sanjo, Yahagi, Ryogoku, Seta, Uji); plank bridges on c3; boat bridge as a rare hero; NONE on c2 (ferry or porters). Stone abutments left standing where a flood took the deck [OL U bridges parts].
types.planting: Levee crests: black or red pine rows, bamboo groves as flood protection, and on the Sumida levee the cherries planted in 1717 under Yoshimune [S-SUMI] (wild types: yamazakura / edohigan, never Somei-yoshino); willows and medake thickets at the water; reeds (yoshi) on the flats; bank willow.
types.buildings: Towns stand back behind the levee; tea stalls on the bridge-end plaza; riverbed shows and stalls on the kawara; houses on stilts over the water at Ryogoku [l14]; outcast hamlets on the flats (neutral).
types.boats: watashi-bune ferry; sanjikkoku-bune (17 x 2.5 m) on the Yodo [S-FSM]; kurawanka food boats at Hirakata; river cargo boats (takasebune) at Kuragano and Kajikazawa; timber rafts (ikada) on the Tenryu, Oi and Tama.
types.abandoned: Autumn low water; a ferry boat stranded high on the gravel, its rope still across the river; one or two bays of a long trestle bridge washed out, leaving pile stumps (a real chokepoint); flotsam piled against the piers; levee grass long and seeded; summer riverbed platforms (Kamo) left as stacked frames on the flats, never set out [S-YUKA]; a porter's platform tipped over on c2.
types.terrain: Levees, kawara gravel flats, braided channels, the bridge-end plaza. This is mostly [terrain].
types.placeable: Bridges, ferry landing, river-works kit (gabions, cribs, groynes), levee steps, boats, water-level post, debris, riverbed platform remains.
types.water: POND for every inland river (stepped pond segments; FEASIBILITY 2.3 says unproven). Rivers at their mouths (Sumida, Yodo at Osaka, Tama at Kawasaki) can be sea-level.

types.water_short: none (gutters, troughs); thin pond strips for d3
types.name: Street-side channel
types.what: Water that runs WITH the street: the stone gutter along house fronts in every town, a wider stone-lined street channel in some post towns, spring-fed streams through a town, hot-water gutters in spa towns.
variants: d1 house-front gutter (omote-dobu): the default in every town; = the jp_s_gutter kit
d2 street channel (yosui): a wider stone channel down the middle or one side of the street, with a slab bridge to each door (Nakatsugawa, Narai troughs, Tsumago, Magome)
d3 spring stream: clear, cold, weedy spring water through town (Mishima, Samegai, Tarui)
d4 hot-water gutter: steaming gutters and troughs in spa towns
d5 plot stream: a small stream crossing each long plot behind the street frontage (Kamiyoshida's Yana-gawa, where pilgrims purified before entering the oshi house)
cross_section: 0.30 wide x 0.25-0.30 deep, stone-lined, 0.3 m outside the house line
jp_s_gutter build list (outdoor kit, W1); Morse figs 33-34 show the stone edge and a slab or board at each door [m033, m034]
Nakatsugawa's channel ran down the centre of the street, fed from the Kurosawa River for fire water; washing in it was forbidden; filled in 1880 [S-NKT]
stone or hollow-log troughs, roofed at Narai
Narai's spring water stations along the street, for drinking and fire [S-NRI]
Mishima's Genbei-gawa, a late-16th-c. channel from Kohama pond, 1.5 km [S-MSM]; Samegai's Jizo-gawa runs ~500 m along the street, ~14 C all year, with baikamo waterweed [S-SMG]
spa-town form; Kusatsu's big trough field (yubatake) needs a date check
Kamiyoshida: Yana-gawa fed from the Sengen shrine; 86 oshi houses on ~750 m of road at the peak [S-KYD]
types.edges: Dressed or rough stone lining; field-stone edges in villages; timber boards on alley drains (dobu-ita).
types.steps_landings: d2/d3: two or three stone steps down to the water at intervals (dipping and washing where allowed); stepping stones across d3.
types.outfalls: d1 ends in an outfall into a canal, river or ditch (jp_s_gutter _outfall).
types.bridges: Stone slab footbridge (1-3 slabs; Morse 268-270) at every door; a plank bridge where a cart crosses d2/d3; gutter slabs on d1.
types.planting: Mostly none; a willow at a corner; baikamo and watercress in d3.
types.buildings: House fronts face the channel; troughs at the inn doors; on d5 the channel crosses each plot in front of the house.
types.abandoned: Silted to half depth with leaves and mud; grass in the joints; a slab tipped into the channel; d2 channels dry or trickling because no one clears the intake (puddles where the silt dams it); a trough overflowing into the street and a wet patch; d3 keeps flowing (springs don't stop) and grows a thick green weed; d4 still steams, with sulphur crust.
types.terrain: The ditch the pieces sit in (a terrain cut or a baked groove); d3 needs a shallow terrain channel.
types.placeable: Gutter pieces (existing kit), wider channel pieces, slab bridges, steps, troughs, spring basins.
types.water: Mostly NO water surface needed: d1/d2 are dry or a decal film. d3 needs thin pond strips (clear-water material). d4: steam particles over a wet decal.

types.water_short: thin pond strips, or dry beds with pools
types.name: Village stream / irrigation channel
types.what: The water every farm village lives on: the main irrigation channel (yosui) threading past the houses from a weir, field ditches, and in the hills a boulder stream with bamboo pipes and log bridges.
variants: e1 lowland: earth-banked irrigation channel, river-stone lined where it passes the houses, sluices, a weir upstream, wash steps
e2 mountain: boulder stream in a narrow valley, dry-stone terraces, bamboo pipes (kakehi) to each house, log and slab bridges
cross_section: earth or stone-lined channel from a weir through the village; also used for washing [OL R 2]
'a channel walled with river stones where it passes the houses, with a step down to the water at each house' [OL R 2]
2-4 steps down to a slab at water level, 0.9-1.8 m wide (assumed)
half-ken or one ken wide; one per house or shared
3-15 m boulder bed, pools and riffles (assumed)
types.edges: Earth banks with grass; river-stone or field-stone walls near houses; stake-and-wattle (shigarami) on bends; gabions (jakago) at the weir.
types.steps_landings: Wash steps (arai-ba) at each house or group; a wooden board-on-posts platform variant; stepping stones.
types.mooring: None (a paddy punt, ta-bune, in delta villages).
types.outfalls: Paddy water notches (mizu-kuchi) and field sluices.
types.bridges: Stone slab footbridge (Morse 268: two slabs set side by side but offset, on stone posts), log bridge, earth-covered bridge (dobashi) for carts, plank bridge.
types.planting: Alders and willows along the paddy bunds (the alder lines carry the autumn hasa racks); bamboo groves behind the farms; persimmon by the house; reeds and water celery in the ditch; red spider lilies on the bunds in autumn (flora list, verify).
types.buildings: Farmhouses sit a few metres back with a wash step, wash tubs and buckets on stakes; the Omi kabata (spring house-basin, Harie) is a lake-shore flavour whose start date is unknown [S-HARIE]: flavour only, flag.
types.boats: Paddy punt (ta-bune) in delta and wajuu villages only.
types.abandoned: Channel choked with weeds and fallen leaves; sluice boards jammed half-open and the field below flooded into a reed marsh (or the paddies dry, harvested stubble); a broken bucket and a rotting wash tub on the wash step; one slab bridge tipped; a treadwheel collapsed on the bank; the weir breached at one end.
types.terrain: Channel cut, paddy terraces, bunds, the weir pool. Mostly [terrain].
types.placeable: Sluice (3 sizes), weir, wash steps, slab and log bridges, stepping stones, bamboo pipe, water lifting (lever sweep, treadwheel), wattle revetment.
types.water: POND strips for the main channel only; field ditches are wet-mud texture. Mountain streams: stepped pond segments or dry boulder beds with pools.

types.name: Castle moat
types.what: The wet or dry moat round a castle, the one waterway every castle town shares.
variants: f1 wet moat: stone wall on the castle side, earth bank or low stone on the town side
f2 dry moat: hill castles and spurs (Komoro, Iida, Takato, Inuyama; Nagoya's honmaru)
f3 concentric round moats: Tanaka only (four rings, ~600 m across) [S-TNK]
cross_section: 20 m typical; 35-50 m big; 70-100 m+ Osaka outer
Himeji: average 20 m, max 34.5 m [S-HMJ]; Matsumoto up to ~50 m [S-MTM]; Osaka's outer moat passed 100 m at its widest [S-HMJ page]
Edo outer moat wall ~6 m [S-EDOM]; Iga Ueno's is famously ~30 m (mem, verify)
turfed earth bank 2-4 m with a low stone or wattle toe (assumed)
types.edges: Ishigaki (KEEP_CIVIC stone rampart; nozura / uchikomi-hagi / kirikomi-hagi as 3 materials, OL 7.17); 'belt' walls (koshimaki / hachimaki: an earth rampart with a stone band at the foot or the top, Edo and Hikone, mem); earth ramparts with turf and pines.
types.steps_landings: Few: a moat-side horse-washing slope (uma-arai-ba) and a boat landing for moat patrol boats (assumed).
types.outfalls: Water gates (sluices) between moat levels; moat dams (dote-bashi) with a path on top [OL U castle].
types.bridges: Earth bridge (dobashi) or plank bridge to each gate (KEEP_CIVIC), sometimes a covered corridor bridge.
types.planting: Pines on the rampart crest and leaning over the water [l11]; lotus in the moat (brown and broken in autumn); reeds in the corners; willow on the town-side bank.
types.buildings: Castle walls, turrets and tamon on top; samurai houses behind board walls on the town side; a guard hut at each gate.
types.boats: A small patrol or maintenance punt (assumed; one per moat).
types.abandoned: Algae-green still water; dead lotus stalks and brown leaves; reeds spreading from the corners; the plank gate bridge rotten with gaps; a punt sunk at the landing; one ishigaki face bulging with a slump of fallen stones.
types.terrain: The moat basin, earth ramparts, the berm (inu-bashiri). Mostly [terrain].
types.placeable: Ishigaki faces (castle kit), earth-bridge ends, plank bridge, water gate, lotus / reed clutter, punt.
types.water: SEA for coastal castles (Kuwana, Osaka, Edo's lower moats); a lake pond where the moat joins a lake (Zeze, Hikone); POND for every other wet moat (flat, one level per moat: the easy case).

types.name: Shore landing (harbour, beach, lake shore)  [NEW TYPE]
types.what: Added because 30+ settlements are ports, fishing villages, salt beaches and lake towns: their water is the sea or a lake, not a canal or river. Kept small: it reuses the canal-edge kit and the shore kit.
variants: g1 harbour quay: stone quay wall, gangi, stone jetty, mooring stones, lighthouse lantern (ports, Miya, Kuwana, Uraga)
g2 beach landing: sand or shingle with boats on skids, capstan, net racks (fishing and salt villages)
g3 lake shore: landing ramp, ferry, jetty on a lake (Lake Biwa, Ashi, Hamana, Suwa)
cross_section: ~8 m wooden tower lantern at Ogaki's river port (1688-1704)
boats drawn up 10-30 m above the waterline (assumed)
types.edges: Dressed stone quays; rough stone breakwaters; natural beach.
types.steps_landings: Gangi (parallel flights along the quay), stone ramps (boat slips), plank jetties on lakes.
types.mooring: Mooring stones and posts; channel stakes (miotsukushi) marking the fairway.
types.planting: Coastal black-pine belt; reeds on lake shores.
types.buildings: Warehouses and boat sheds; houses gable-end to the beach in fishing villages.
types.boats: Fishing boats and beached boats (shore kit), tenmasen lighters, ferry boats; big cargo ships at anchor as landmarks.
types.abandoned: Boats hauled up and left to rot or overturned; a swamped boat at the quay; nets rotted on the racks; driftwood and wrack piled on the quay steps; the lantern's paper gone.
types.terrain: Beach, quay platform, harbour basin. Mostly [terrain].
types.placeable: Wall modules, gangi, mooring kit, lighthouse lantern, jetty, boats and shore kit (KEEP_OUTDOOR 'Shore and salt').
types.water: SEA for coast; POND (lake) for Biwa / Ashi / Suwa; Hamana is brackish and joined to the sea since 1498, so SEA-level works.

S-TAK.what: Takase River: canal 1611, ~10 km; ~8 m channel, ~30 cm water; takasebune ~13 x 2 m, 15 koku; ~200 boats, ~700 haulers; 9 funairi, Ichi-no-funairi 55 x 6 ken, stone-walled

S-OSK.what: Osaka canals: Higashi-yokobori 1585, Nishi-yokobori 1600, Dotonbori 1612-15 (30-50 m today), Edobori 1617, Nagahori ~40 m

S-KURA.what: Hiroshima domain kura-yashiki, Nakanoshima, Osaka (excavated 1995-2018): stone revetment ~3 m high, gangi, boat basin 51 x 47 m cut into the plot

S-30K.what: Sanjukkenbori (Edo): dug 1612, ~30 ken (~55 m) wide, quays both sides; narrowed to 19 ken in 1828

S-KAMO.what: Kamo River: Kanbun new levee completed 1670, river narrowed to ~100 m, straightened, stone revetment; Sanjo Ohashi 61 x 3 ken (1780 record)

S-YAH.what: Yahagi-bashi, Okazaki: 208 ken (~378 m), a shogunal bridge, first built 1601; longest on the Tokaido

S-SUMI.what: Sumida levee (Bokutei) cherries planted by Yoshimune, usually dated 1717 (other dates proposed)

S-NGY.what: Nagoya Horikawa: dug 1610 by Fukushima Masanori, castle to Atsuta, ~6 km, 12-48 ken (22-87 m); merchant kura upstream of Nayabashi, domain rice stores below

S-OGK.what: Ogaki: Suimon-gawa boats via the Ibi to Kuwana; Funamachi river port; Sumiyoshi lantern ~8 m, built 1688-1704; Basho left by boat in 1689

S-ISE.what: Ise Kawasaki: kura and townhouses on both banks of the Seta River, goods moved straight from boats into the kura; Isuzu mitarashi stone paving given by Keishoin

S-NKT.what: Nakatsugawa post town: a water channel down the centre of the main street past the honjin, for fire; washing forbidden; filled and moved in 1880; shown on the Nakasendo survey map

S-NRI.what: Narai post town: spring-water stations along the street for drinking and fire; one roofed with stone-weighted boards

S-MSM.what: Mishima: Genbei-gawa, a 1.5 km channel from Kohama pond dug for paddies in the late 16th c.; on the shogunate's road survey map

S-FSM.what: Fushimi: jikkoku and sanjikkoku boats between Fushimi and Osaka; sanjikkoku-bune ~17 x 2.5 m (another source: 11-15 x ~2 m in the Genroku era)

S-YODO.what: Yodo castle waterwheels: two, 8 and 6 ken across, lifting river water into the castle

S-KRG.what: Kuragano kashi on the Karasu River: the uppermost Tone river port, shogunate-approved in the early Edo period; takasebune to Edo

S-NMZ.what: Numazu castle built 1777-79 by Mizuno Tadatomo; Sanmaibashi castle abandoned 1614

S-TNK.what: Tanaka castle, Fujieda: concentric circular plan ~600 m across, four moat rings; Honda lords from 1730

S-HMJ.what: Himeji castle moats: average 20 m, max 34.5 m, depth ~2.7 m (a generic Edo-period wet-moat benchmark)

S-MTM.what: Matsumoto castle: three rings of wide moats, ~50 m wide east of the main gate

S-EDOM.what: Edo castle outer moat (1636): stone wall ~6 m high on the Nihonbashi River's south bank; excavated moat walls stand on timber sills with piles ~1 m apart

S-YUKA.what: Kamo riverbed cooling platforms: from the early modern period; by the mid-Edo ~400 tea shops with benches on the flats and shallows (kawara no suzumi). Summer only

S-HARIE.what: Harie (Takashima, Omi) kabata spring-water house basins; origin date not given

S-KST.what: Kusatsu River: a raised-bed (tenjo) river; the bed built up mostly from the late 1700s to 1886; the road climbed over it until the 1886 tunnel

S-SMG.what: Samegai: the Jizo-gawa from the Isame spring runs ~500 m through the post town, ~14 C all year, baikamo waterweed

S-KYD.what: Kamiyoshida oshi town: founded 1572; 86 oshi lodges on ~750 m of road at the peak; the Yana-gawa stream in front of each house where Fuji pilgrims purified
